Design settings

Basic · Actions Stable

Comment control

Where do I start commenting on this page, and how many comments are here?

2 variants × 4 states · 2 toggles
Open threads
3 (sample)
Other slides
5 open threads elsewhere in the deck, shown by the mark (sample)
Shortcut
⇧⌥C on a Mac (sample)

Point at the tag, or Tab to it: the shortcut slides out to the left and the tag stays put. Enter or Space turns comment mode on, which fills it with the spot colour. Turn on With count to show the number of open threads in place of the comment icon, and With mark for the dot that says other slides of a deck have threads too.

Used in composites

No composite uses it yet.

Used on screens

Field notes · October

Autumn at the footbridge

What we found at the footbridge, and what to do before winter.

RFRed Fox9m ago

Lead with the recommendation; the finding can follow.

The river

The river , and both times the footbridge held. The second rise came within a hand of the deck boards, which is closer than any year since the bridge was rebuilt.

MLMaya Lindqvist3m ago

Was it twice? The log says once, on the 14th.

We recommend raising the deck by one course before the spring melt. The cost is modest and the work can be done in two days with the water low.

MLMaya Lindqvist5m ago

Two days is optimistic. Last time the same job took a week; say so, or give a range.

The path

RFRed Foxjust now

Walkers need a sign here before the meadow is gone.

The path on the north bank is washed out for about twenty metres. Walkers are cutting across the meadow, which is doing more harm than the river did.

Prompt to build this component

When to use it

When to use

  • As the one small control Pipeup adds to a page: tucked into the page's bottom-right corner, it starts and stops comment mode, counts the open threads and opens the menu.
  • Once per page, never more.

When not to use

  • For any other action on the page: use cmp-button or cmp-icon-button.
  • To show a count on its own: use cmp-status-pill.
Variants, anatomy, accessibility, interaction and content rules

Variants

  • default — a small square tag flush to the corner, ink on paper with a hard shadow, showing the comment mark; the base class alone, no modifier class.
  • corner — the same, as the last thing in a page's stack: it sticks to the bottom-right corner of the window, flush with both edges, only its top-left corner rounded, and stays there as the page scrolls.

Anatomy

  • Root: <button class="ds-comment-control" type="button" aria-pressed="false" aria-label="<Comments: n open. Start commenting (shortcut)>">; add ds-comment-control--corner on a page.
  • Mark: <span class="ds-icon" data-icon="chat-circle"></span>, shown while there are no open threads.
  • Count (with-count): <span class="ds-comment-control__count">3</span>, the number of open threads inside the mark's place, at most two characters ("9+"); it replaces the mark.
  • Mark (with-mark): <span class="ds-comment-control__mark"></span>, a small dot at the tag's top-left corner that shows when other slides of a deck have open threads; the label says how many ("2 here · 5 on other slides").
  • Reach: <span class="ds-comment-control__reach">⇧⌥C</span>, the shortcut that slides out to the left while the control is pointed at or focused; the control itself never moves.

Accessibility

  • A native <button> with aria-pressed for comment mode, so Enter and Space toggle it and screen readers hear "pressed" when comment mode is on.
  • Its aria-label carries the exact count, the state and the shortcut, so the "9+" is never the only reading.
  • The reach is decorative for assistive technology (aria-hidden="true"); the shortcut is in the label.
  • The square meets the minimum target in every density, and is 44 px on touch screens.

Interaction

  • Hover and focus slide the reach out to the left over --ds-motion-settle on --ds-motion-ease (its width and opacity ease) and darken the paper over --ds-motion-quick (int-01, int-02, int-03).
  • Press shifts the fill over --ds-motion-quick; nothing changes size.
  • on (comment mode) fills the tag with the accent colour over --ds-motion-quick; the mark and count turn to the on-accent text.
  • Focus shows the shared ring (int-02). Under reduced motion the reach appears in place (int-06).

Content rules

  • The count is a number up to 9, then "9+", and on a deck it counts the open threads on this slide. The label says the exact numbers: "Comments: 12 open", or on a deck "2 here · 5 on other slides".
  • The reach shows only the shortcut as the keyboard labels it: ⇧⌥C on a Mac, Shift+Alt+C elsewhere.

Do and don't

  • Do keep it flush to the corner and 32 px square; it is a tag on the page, not a button in it.
  • Don't add words to the tag; its menu and its label say the rest.
  • Don't move it when the reach slides out.
Source: design-system/components/basic/cmp-comment-control/
